subtitle: Mexican red rice
verso: Don't even look at the rice: cover it and leave it be.
story: Fried until golden before any liquid goes in, then cooked in tomato broth and left alone. It goes next to everything, and into soup.

ingredients.title: Rice
items: 1 carrot, diced, and ½ cup peas, optional

steps: Soak the rice in hot water 10 minutes. Rinse until the water runs clear, then drain very well.
Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium. Add the rice and stir until it turns opaque and light golden and sounds like sand, about 8 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic with [[½ cup]] of the broth. Strain onto the rice and stir 2–3 minutes, until absorbed and the color deepens.
Add the rest of the broth, the salt, carrot, peas, cilantro and serrano. Bring to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to its lowest setting and cook 18 minutes. Don't lift the lid or stir.
Turn off the heat and let rest 10 minutes, covered. Fluff with a fork.

pressureCooker.time: 4 min high pressure + 10 min natural release
steps: Soak, rinse and drain the rice. Fry it in the oil on Sauté until golden.
Add the strained tomato purée and stir 2 minutes.
Add broth so the total liquid (purée plus broth) is [[1¾ cups]], then the salt, vegetables, cilantro and serrano. Scrape the bottom well so it won't set off the burn warning.
High pressure 4 minutes, natural release 10. Fluff.

tips: Plenty of grandmas swap some of the salt for a spoon of Knorr tomato bouillon. Nobody has to know.
Lifting the lid lets out the steam, and you get rice that's raw on top and mushy underneath.

variations.name: Arroz Verde
variations.subtitle: Green poblano rice
variations.note: The same method with a green purée instead of tomato.

items: The same rice, broth and method as the base

steps: Fry the rice as in the base.
Add the green purée instead of the tomato and cook 2 minutes.
Continue with the broth as in the base.
variations.pressureNote: Same pressure time as the base.
